facebook.long_form:
📅 Four days. The 2026-27 NBA schedule drops Thursday, August 13 — and the Christmas Day speculation alone is worth the wait.

The NBA Cup (Emirates NBA Cup) slate arrives first on Tuesday, August 11. Then Thursday, we get all 1,230 regular-season games for all 30 teams.

Here's what has the entire basketball world buzzing right now:

**Christmas Day.** The league hasn't officially confirmed the Christmas matchups yet, but the ingredients are historic. LeBron James is now in Philadelphia. Giannis Antetokounmpo is in Miami. Victor Wembanyama is in San Antonio. The Knicks are the defending champions. That's four franchise-level stories all pointing to one five-game Christmas slate. Every NBA fan has an opinion on who faces who.

**LeBron's Philly debut.** In 21 previous seasons, LeBron has worn the Cavaliers, Heat, and Lakers. Thursday reveals when — and where — he first suits up as a Philadelphia 76er. The road opener in New York or Boston will be circled on every opponent's calendar the moment the schedule drops.

**The Knicks' banner night.** Defending champions open October 20 at Madison Square Garden. The opponent gets the most-watched regular-season opener in the East. Every team's PR department is quietly rooting for (or against) the assignment.

**Wemby vs. Embiid dates.** Two of the most compelling big men in the league, in different conferences — the rare dates they share a court are events.

This is the most star-loaded schedule reveal in recent memory. Thursday can't come soon enough.

💬 Which game are you circling the moment the schedule drops?

stories.angle: ESPN reports the NBA's salary cap investigation into the Clippers and Kawhi Leonard could extend into 2027, adding a new urgency to the Raptors-Clippers trade saga. The probe centers on a $28M Aspiration endorsement deal the Clippers allegedly facilitated. With training camp seven weeks away, the Raptors' trade calculation grows more complicated by the day.

facebook.long_form:
⚖️ The most complicated trade in NBA history just got a new timeline: 2027.

ESPN is reporting that the NBA's salary cap investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers and Kawhi Leonard could extend into next year. That is a staggering development — because training camp opens in approximately seven weeks.

Here's the full picture:

**The deal:** In late June, the Clippers and Toronto Raptors agreed to a blockbuster trade. Kawhi Leonard goes to Toronto. In return, the Clippers get Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, and two unprotected first-round picks (2031 and 2033). The deal is currently frozen.

**The investigation:** The probe centers on a $28 million endorsement deal between Leonard and Aspiration — a green bank that also held a $300 million, 23-year deal with the Clippers franchise. Aspiration has since gone bankrupt. The NBA is investigating whether the Clippers used that deal to effectively compensate Leonard outside the salary cap system.

**The complication:** The NBPA has warned it "wouldn't hesitate" to demand neutral arbitration if the league pursues penalties without sufficient evidence. Any arbitration ruling would then face a three-person appeals panel jointly appointed by both sides. There is no hard deadline. That process could — per ESPN — run all the way into 2027.

**What this means for Toronto:** The Raptors have been told they'll assume the risk of any investigation outcome if they choose to finalize the trade before the probe concludes. That's an enormous liability to take on — they could complete the trade and then have it unwound or have Kawhi face a suspension. So they wait.

Kawhi Leonard is owed $50.3 million in 2026-27. He is a Clipper with no team to play for. Seven weeks to training camp.

The clock is ticking — very slowly. 🕐

---

stories.title: Stephen Curry — On Track to Be First NBA Player to Earn $60M in a Single Season
stories.angle: When Curry signs his expected 2-year, $136.7M extension on or after August 29, his 2026-27 salary will combine his existing $65M contract with extension-year money — potentially making him the first NBA player to surpass $60M in a single season. The Warriors are ready to offer the full max. A September signing is widely expected.

x_posts.text:

When he signs the expected 2yr/$136.7M max, his 2026-27 earnings could make him the first NBA player to surpass $60M in a single season.

No player has ever done it. Steph would be the first. #Warriors #NBA

facebook.long_form:
💰 Stephen Curry is about to do something no NBA player has ever done.

When Curry's extension window opens August 29, the Warriors are prepared to offer the full two-year, $136.7 million maximum deal. Per CBS Sports, the extension structure — layered on top of his existing $65 million 2026-27 salary — would make Curry the first NBA player in history to earn more than $60 million in a single season.

Let that land: sixty. million. dollars. In one year.

To put it in context: in 2003, LeBron James signed his first NBA contract for $18.8 million — his entire four-year rookie deal. The max salary has evolved with the salary cap, but Curry surpassing $60 million in a single season is a genuine historical marker for how dramatically the NBA's economics have changed.

Here's the situation heading into the extension window:

Curry is 38 years old. He finished the 2025-26 season as one of the most efficient shooters in the league despite Golden State's 37-45 record. The Warriors have retooled around him with Draymond Green (1yr/$27.7M) and Gary Payton II (1yr/$3.9M) both re-signed. Curry has no interest in leaving Golden State — multiple sources confirm he is finishing his career there. The extension, which should be signed in September, locks that in through the 2027-28 season.

Without the extension, Curry becomes an unrestricted free agent next summer for the first time in his career. The Warriors have absolutely no intention of letting that happen.

For the record books and for Warriors fans: August 29 opens the window. September closes the deal.

---

France opens against Serbia in Belgrade on August 20, then again in Orleans on August 23, before crucial World Cup qualifiers vs. Slovenia and Sweden. facebook.long_form:
🇫🇷 Victor Wembanyama is going home — and the return is only 11 days away.

After two years away from the French national team, Wembanyama rejoins Les Bleus for a summer that includes two exhibitions against Serbia and a pair of crucial 2027 World Cup qualifying games. New France head coach Frederic Fauthoux — who replaced Vincent Collet after the Paris Olympics — will be coaching Wembanyama at the national team level for the very first time.

Here's the August schedule:

- **August 20** — Exhibition vs. Serbia (Belgrade)
- **August 23** — Exhibition vs. Serbia (Orleans)
- **August 27** — 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifier vs. Slovenia (home)
- **August 30** — 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifier at Sweden (away)

France currently leads Group L with a 5-1 record after the first qualifying round. The August games are critical for securing qualification to the 2027 World Cup. Add Wembanyama, Rudy Gobert, and Evan Fournier to a team already 5-1 — this is one of the most dangerous national teams in the world.

Wembanyama's quote says it all: "I don't miss the NBA at the moment, but I do miss FIBA." That's not a knock on the NBA — it's a testament to how much he loves the international game. The pace. The teamwork. The way FIBA basketball is played.

And now, Spurs coaches and staff made the trip to Paris too, investing in Wembanyama's development even through the national team window. That kind of organizational commitment is rare.

The NBA won't start for another 72 days. But for basketball fans paying attention, August 20 in Belgrade is must-watch.

---

stories.title: LeBron "Trusts the Process" — Embiid's Transformation Has the NBA Talking
stories.angle: When Joel Embiid posted an offseason photo showing a dramatically leaner physique, LeBron James reposted it with the caption "Trust The Process!" — a callback to the 76ers' legendary rebuild era. The moment went viral, capping a summer in which Embiid has completed his first full offseason program without restrictions in years. 76ers president Mike Gansey confirmed it: Embiid is healthy going into training camp.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:

"One of the first offseasons he is healthy going in." #Sixers #NBA

facebook.long_form:
🔁 "Trust The Process."

Three words. LeBron James posted them as a reaction to Joel Embiid's offseason photo. The internet has not stopped talking about it since.

Embiid posted a photo this summer showing a dramatically transformed physique — visibly leaner, more conditioned than he's been in years. The 76ers' medical staff and front office have been transparent about his progress: president Mike Gansey confirmed that Embiid has completed "one of the first offseasons he is healthy going into it" — a full program, no restrictions.

For LeBron to respond with "Trust The Process" — the phrase coined during Philadelphia's infamous tank era under Sam Hinkie — is a full-circle cultural moment. The 76ers spent years "trusting the process" through seasons of deliberately bad basketball in pursuit of future stars. Now LeBron James, in the final chapter of his career, has joined that franchise. The process has arrived.

The broader picture is remarkable. Philadelphia's projected starting five: LeBron James. Joel Embiid. Tyrese Maxey. Jaylen Brown. Jared Edgecombe. That's five combined MVP awards, a two-time Finals MVP, and one of the most talented defensive prospects in years. All on the same team.

Maxey has been in the gym at 6 AM before LeBron shows up. LeBron is leaving the gym before the sun is fully up. Embiid is in his best shape in years. Brown is adapting from a championship culture in Boston to a new superstar-laden locker room.

Training camp doesn't open until late September. The 76ers are already operating like a team with something to prove.

Trust the process — it's just getting started. 🏀

---
